items.title: Nobody Wants Your Damn App
items.summary: Nobody wants another app cluttering their phone—so why does every website keep begging us to install one? The web already perfected the experience: click, load, done. Maybe it’s time we stopped trying to ruin it.

items.title: Web-Perf Wednesday 010 – Safari Keeps Scrolled Content in Place
items.summary: Safari 27 adds scroll anchoring, tighter HTTP caching, and static Service Worker routes, while Chrome improves performance tooling.

items.title: I rebuilt 0xinsider around Polymarket sports and esports data
items.summary: 0xinsider is now Polymarket analytics for sports and esports. What 149,700 wallets and 411,770 large buys say, with every query public.

items.title: I added Agentic Resource Discovery to 0xinsider so agents can find it
items.summary: ARD is a new proposal from Google, Microsoft and Hugging Face for how agents find tools. What's in it, what 0xinsider publishes, and what a registry returns.

items.title: This Weird 1973 Typeface Just Came Back From the Dead
items.summary: A wonderfully weird typeface from 1973 has come back to life — and somehow it looks more at home in 2026 than ever. Meet Clippy, the retro font that bends, rocks and wobbles its way into the digital age.

items.title: The Death of Apps Has Already Begun
items.summary: We spent 15 years filling our phones with apps. AI could make almost all of them invisible... and the death of apps may already be closer than anyone realizes.

items.title: Periodic Table of HTML Elements
items.summary: Periodic Table of HTML Elements shows all 115 HTML elements laid out as a periodic table. Josh Duck created the original periodic table of HTML elements that I included in my Atomic Design book. Thankfully, Alena Batitskaia recreated it updated to the latest spec!

items.title: AI Can Build Your UI. Now Figma Can Tell It When It Screwed Up.
items.summary: AI can now build a UI in seconds, but that doesn't mean it built the UI you actually designed. A new Applitools integration turns Figma designs into visual baselines, automatically catching the subtle differences AI coding agents leave behind before they make it into production.

items.title: 25 Places Designers Can Still Find Free, Non-AI Images for Commercial Use
items.summary: AI images are taking over stock libraries, but the human-made web isn't dead yet. We found 25 places where designers can still find incredible free, real photography, art, and imagery for commercial use.

items.title: Chrome Can Now Measure Exactly How Obnoxious Your Website’s Ads Are
items.summary: Chrome can now measure exactly how obnoxious a website’s ads are, from how much of your screen they swallow to how much data and CPU time they burn. Those ad-stuffed websites can finally be measured, and the results are public.

items.title: Cloudflare Just Gave AI Training Bots the Middle Finger
items.summary: Cloudflare just gave website owners a new weapon against AI crawlers: keep the search traffic, block the AI training. After years of watching bots consume the web’s content, publishers finally have an easier way to tell AI companies where to go.

items.title: Today, WordPress Ended a 16-Year Tradition… Meet Ipsum!
items.summary: After 16 years, WordPress just killed one of its most recognizable traditions. The predictable “Twenty Something” default themes are history, and their replacement, Ipsum, signals a surprisingly different vision for what WordPress thinks a modern website should start with.

items.title: Photoshop Elements 2027 Adds AI Assistant, Generative Expand, and Upscale
items.summary: Photoshop Elements is getting a serious AI upgrade, with Generative Expand, AI upscaling and a new assistant that helps you edit simply by describing what you want.

items.title: Web-Perf Wednesday 009 – CrUX Makes Ad Weight Public
items.summary: CrUX adds public ad count, density, CPU, and network metrics, giving publishers and advertisers a shared view of real ad weight.

items.title: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Has a Left-Handed Problem
items.summary: Apple moved key controls to the side of its new foldable iPhone to make them easier to reach — but easier for whom? The decision raises a surprisingly big UX question that every web and interface designer should be thinking about.

items.title: Figma Is Turning Designers Into Plugin Makers
items.summary: Figma is turning a wild idea into reality: instead of searching for the perfect plugin, you can just ask AI to build it. If this catches on, designers may stop choosing the tools in their software—and start inventing them on demand.

items.summary: After 53 years working with type, Pat Lightizer got the ultimate retirement gift: her own font.
